_methodology_note: The local-side numbers below are full-scale and freshly verified: routing_accuracy ran the complete 49-query eval set, retrieval_quality ran the complete 14-hard-query x 3-user set (n=42) -- confirmed reproducible across three consecutive full-scale runs after root-causing and fixing the resource-accumulation hang (see REPORT.md section 5.6 for the full investigation: it was Ollama's own llama-server accumulating state across ~90+ sequential requests in one process, not a Python-side leak -- fixed by running each (backend, phase) pair in its own subprocess). Cloud routing accuracy was not obtained this session: the free-tier Gemini rate limit caused the routing subprocess to exceed its 900s budget twice in a row; this is caught gracefully now (see the TimeoutExpired handling in eval/local_vs_cloud.py) rather than crashing, but a real number still requires either a paid tier or a very long wait. This is the well-documented, pre-existing rate-limit constraint from REPORT.md section 8.1, not a new issue. Cloud retrieval-quality reuses the already-real, already-validated hard-tier result (42 runs) from eval/results/retrieval_quality_summary.json, generated earlier in this project with the cloud backend against the same eval set and difficulty slice -- not a fresh run of this exact script, but a genuine cloud-backend number, not a placeholder.

cloud.note: Not obtained this session -- free-tier rate limit exceeded the 900s subprocess budget on repeated attempts.
